title: Color a Map: Paint Countries Your Way
description: Color a Map lets you paint countries in your own colours with a click, track what you have coloured, and export the result or the list. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a student planning a gap year paints the 12 countries on the route in green, the maybes in yellow and the noes in red — then exports the list as a CSV packing checklist.
quick_answer: Color a Map turns a world outline into a click-to-paint canvas: choose a colour, click countries to fill them, and watch your coloured list grow. Export the picture for a slide or the country list as CSV when you are done — no account, everything in your browser.

popular_table.title: Colour schemes that read well
popular_table.intro: Four or five well-chosen colours beat twelve random ones. These patterns cover most jobs.
rows: Teal = visited, light grey = not yet
One distinct hue per group, grey for none
Green = going, yellow = maybe, red = not this time
popular_table.note: Keep uncoloured countries a light neutral rather than white-on-white, and remember colour-blind readers: avoid red-versus-green as your only distinction where the map carries real information.

faq: Can I colour US states or counties instead of countries?
This canvas is the world of countries. For American geography, start from a Blank Map of US states for hand colouring, or the US County Choropleth when you have real per-county numbers.
How many colours do I get?
A working palette sized for map sense — enough for categories and scales without turning the map into confetti. If you need a specific brand colour precisely, a drawing program is the better tool.
Yes — click it again with the clear/eraser choice (or cycle back to uncoloured) and the list updates. Mistakes cost one click, which is the point of doing this digitally.
Does it count my countries for me?
The coloured list tracks as you paint, including a count per colour — handy for the 'how many have I visited?' question that starts most sessions.
What format is the image export?
A PNG of your coloured map, sized for slides and documents. The list export is CSV: country, colour — ready for a spreadsheet.
Why do small island nations look like dots?
At world scale they are dots. Zoom toward the Pacific or Caribbean before clicking, or accept the list entry without a visible fill at poster zoom.
Can two people colour the same map?
Not simultaneously — there is no shared live canvas and no account system. Export your version and send the file; collaboration here is deliberately file-based.
